Collision checking at a configuration

Source: R/collision.R
robot_check_collision.Rd

Checks the robot's collision geometry against the obstacles of an environment and, with self = TRUE, against itself. Self-collision skips link pairs that no movable joint separates, and pairs separated by one movable joint when no link between them carries collision geometry (joint neighbors, possibly through geometry-free fixed frames); a tool fixed to a link is still checked against the link before that link's joint. Further link pairs can be excluded with ignore_pairs. A cheap bounding-sphere test prunes pairs that are farther apart than margin. This checks one configuration only: a collision-free start and goal do not imply that the motion between them is collision-free; use robot_check_path() for that.

Usage

robot_check_collision(
  robot,
  q,
  environment = NULL,
  self = TRUE,
  margin = 0,
  ignore_pairs = NULL,
  distances = FALSE
)

Arguments

robot

A robot_model with collision geometry.

q

Configuration.

environment

Optional robot_environment.

self

Check self-collision.

margin

Safety margin: pairs closer than margin count as colliding.

ignore_pairs

Optional list of c(link_a, link_b) name pairs to skip in self-collision checking.

distances

Compute exact distances for every pair (slower).

Value

A robot_collision_result with in_collision, min_distance (over evaluated pairs, NA if none) and a data frame pairs of evaluated pairs.

Examples

robot <- robot_capsule_links(robot_example("planar2"), 0.05)
env <- robot_environment(box = geom_box(c(0.4, 0.4, 0.4),
                                        origin = transl(1.5, 0, 0)))
robot_check_collision(robot, c(0, 0), env)$in_collision
#> [1] TRUE
robot_check_collision(robot, c(pi / 2, 0), env)$in_collision
#> [1] FALSE
